title: Urea water bath treatment for monogenean parasites in hagfish
author: Tomita, Takaoka, et al.

steps.title: Prepare urea bath
steps.instruction: Fill a 30‑L plastic container placed next to the seawater tank with 10 L of urea water (the same solution used in the study).

steps.title: Transfer hagfish to bath
steps.instruction: Move each infected hagfish from the seawater tank into the prepared urea‑water container.

steps.title: Bathe for five minutes
steps.instruction: Keep the hagfish in the urea‑water bath for exactly 5 min.

steps.title: Return fish to seawater
steps.instruction: After the 5‑min exposure, return the hagfish to their original seawater tanks (maintained at 8 °C).

description: The applicability of urea water as a parasiticidal bathing fluid has so far only been confirmed in hagfish and the applicability to other fish taxa still remains unknown. However, we expect that urea water baths would also be applicable as a parasiticidal to elasmobranchs (sharks and batoids), which are less tolerant of hypoosmotic environments compared to teleosts, and for which freshwater baths are not suitable. Our preliminary experiments have confirmed that the two host species of shark (Scyliorhinus tokubee and Mustelus manazo) can tolerate the 5-min exposure to urea water. Survival tests in the urea water for the monogenean parasites that are isolated from infected elasmobranchs, as demonstrated in Fig. 2, are the next step towards evaluating the applicability of the parasiticidal method evaluated in the present study.
